split_reasoning: Test plans and detailed test cases or scripts are different deliverables, even though both support testing.

parts.text: Design a test plan for a software change or release.
parts.type_reasoning: A completed test plan is a distinct artifact used by the test team.
parts.unit_reasoning: A plan for one release or change is reviewed and used as a whole.
parts.start: requirements and scope for the change or release are available
parts.end: test plan is prepared and shared for review or use

parts.text: Design test scenarios, scripts, or procedures for software functionality.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces documented test designs that testers can execute.
parts.unit_reasoning: A related set of cases or scripts is handed over for a feature or test objective.
parts.work_item: one feature-level set of test cases or scripts
parts.start: feature requirements or test objectives are available
parts.end: cases or scripts are ready for review and execution

notes: The boundary between a plan and detailed cases varies by team; time shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: Testing modifications is one activity, regardless of the particular change under test.

parts.text: Test a system modification before implementation.
parts.type_reasoning: A test run produces results that the release team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: Results for one modification or release candidate are reviewed together for implementation.
parts.work_item: one modification test run and its results
parts.start: modified build and applicable tests are available
parts.end: tests are executed and results recorded for the release team

notes: Defect reporting is separately covered by task 14641.

split_reasoning: The listed testing areas are alternative coverage targets for developing a testing program, not separate activities.

parts.text: Develop a testing program covering the relevant software risks and scenarios.
parts.type_reasoning: A testing program is a defined set of tests and coverage used by a project team.
parts.unit_reasoning: The program for a release or feature is assembled and reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one testing program for a release or feature
parts.start: scope, requirements, and testing risks are available
parts.end: test coverage and associated tests are prepared for use

notes: Testing programs may range from organized suites of cases to more formal programs depending on the workplace.

split_reasoning: Documenting and reporting a defect are connected steps in producing one bug report.

parts.text: Document a software defect in the bug tracker and report it to developers.
parts.type_reasoning: Each defect yields a tracker entry that developers act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: The individual bug ticket is the unit assigned and tracked.
parts.start: a suspected defect and supporting evidence are identified
parts.end: bug ticket is entered and made available to the responsible developers

split_reasoning: Function, output, screens, and content are alternative places where the same problem-analysis activity occurs.

parts.text: Identify, analyze, and document a problem in software behavior or content.
parts.type_reasoning: Each investigation produces a documented problem and supporting analysis.
parts.unit_reasoning: A single identified problem is the unit passed to others for review or correction.
parts.work_item: one software problem analyzed and documented
parts.start: anomalous behavior, output, screen, or content is observed
parts.end: problem and analysis are documented for review

notes: The documentation may be a bug ticket, but the target also includes identifying and analyzing the problem.

split_reasoning: Monitoring resolution and tracking success are parts of following a defect through its status changes.

parts.text: Track the progress and outcome of a defect resolution effort.
parts.type_reasoning: Continuous monitoring produces individual defect-status updates that others rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A tracked defect is the unit whose resolution progress and outcome are followed.
parts.start: a tracked defect is due for follow-up or its status changes
parts.end: current progress or outcome is recorded or communicated
parts.checked_by: test lead, developers, and project manager

notes: Verifying a fix may be handled in a separate test run; this item covers tracking its outcome.

split_reasoning: Creating a defect database and maintaining its contents are distinct deliverables.

parts.text: Create a database for known test defects.
parts.type_reasoning: A configured database is a distinct resource used by the test team.
parts.unit_reasoning: The configured database is handed over as a working resource.
parts.start: requirements for storing and accessing defect information are identified
parts.end: database is configured and available for use

parts.text: Maintain the accuracy and organization of a known-defect database.
parts.type_reasoning: Maintenance produces updated defect records others use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A batch of record updates can be reviewed and relied on as a completed maintenance pass.
parts.work_item: one batch of defect database updates
parts.start: new or changed defect information is available for database maintenance
parts.end: affected records are updated or reconciled

notes: Shares depend on whether the organization already has a defect-tracking system.

split_reasoning: Scheduling and strategy are related planning components of a test effort, normally assembled together.

parts.text: Plan a test schedule or strategy around project scope and delivery dates.
parts.type_reasoning: The planning produces an agreed schedule or strategy used to coordinate testing.
parts.unit_reasoning: A project or release-level testing schedule or strategy is reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: project scope and delivery constraints are available
parts.end: schedule or strategy is prepared and shared with the project team

split_reasoning: The listed subjects are different inputs to the same product design review interaction.

parts.text: Participate in a product design review and provide testing-related input.
parts.type_reasoning: The target is participation and discussion in a live review.

notes: Any separately prepared review document is not specified by the target.

split_reasoning: Accuracy, compliance, completeness, and risk are different review criteria applied to the same documentation.

parts.text: Review software documentation for quality, compliance, and risk.
parts.type_reasoning: The review produces comments or a reviewed document that authors can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A document or defined document section is normally submitted for review as a unit.
parts.start: document is submitted for review
parts.end: review comments or approval are returned to the author

split_reasoning: Replicability and standards compliance are purposes of the same procedure-documentation activity.

parts.text: Document a test procedure so it can be repeated and meets applicable standards.
parts.type_reasoning: The documented procedure is an artifact used by testers and reviewers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A procedure for a defined test activity is maintained and reviewed as a unit.
parts.start: test method and applicable standards are available
parts.end: procedure is documented and made available for review or use
parts.checked_by: testers, test lead, and compliance reviewers

notes: This covers documenting the procedure, not necessarily designing the full test plan.

split_reasoning: Quality standards and the methods or procedures used to apply them are different deliverables.

parts.text: Develop or specify product quality or release-readiness standards.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces criteria that a team can review and apply.
parts.unit_reasoning: A set of quality or readiness criteria is approved and used together.
parts.work_item: one set of quality or release-readiness standards
parts.start: quality objectives and applicable requirements are identified
parts.end: standards are specified and submitted for review

parts.text: Develop or specify methods or procedures for assessing product quality or release readiness.
parts.type_reasoning: The work produces an assessment method or procedure used by others.
parts.unit_reasoning: An assessment procedure for a defined quality or readiness decision is reviewed as a unit.
parts.work_item: one quality or release-readiness assessment procedure
parts.start: assessment objectives and applicable criteria are available
parts.end: method or procedure is documented and submitted for review

notes: A workplace may combine standards and procedures in one document; shares are estimates.

split_reasoning: Updating automated scripts is one activity regardless of what changed in the software.

parts.text: Update automated test scripts to reflect current software and requirements.
parts.type_reasoning: The updated scripts are distinct artifacts used in subsequent testing.
parts.unit_reasoning: A related set of script changes for a feature or software change is typically reviewed together.
parts.work_item: one set of automated test script updates
parts.start: software change or obsolete script behavior is identified
parts.end: scripts are updated, checked, and submitted for use
parts.checked_by: test automation lead and other testers

split_reasoning: Investigating a referred customer problem is one activity, irrespective of the cause.

parts.text: Investigate a customer problem referred by technical support.
parts.type_reasoning: The referred case produces investigation findings that support staff or developers use.
parts.unit_reasoning: The referred support case is the unit received and returned with findings.
parts.start: technical support refers a customer case with available evidence
parts.end: findings or recommended next steps are returned to support or developers

notes: This codes the referred investigation, not a live support conversation.

split_reasoning: Installing, maintaining, and using testing software produce different outputs and are distinct activities.

parts.text: Install a software testing program.
parts.type_reasoning: Installation produces a configured program available for testing.
parts.unit_reasoning: One installation is completed and checked as a usable setup.
parts.start: testing software and installation requirements are available
parts.end: program is installed and basic operation is verified

parts.text: Maintain a software testing program.
parts.type_reasoning: Maintenance produces an updated or repaired testing tool configuration.
parts.unit_reasoning: A maintenance change or update is applied and verified as a unit.
parts.start: an update, configuration change, or tool problem is identified
parts.end: maintenance change is applied and checked

parts.text: Use a software testing program to execute tests.
parts.type_reasoning: A testing session produces results that the test team uses.
parts.unit_reasoning: A test run or suite execution produces a coherent set of results.
parts.work_item: one test suite run using a testing program
parts.start: test build, test suite, and testing program are ready
parts.end: suite is executed and results are available

notes: Shares vary substantially with the availability and ownership of testing tools.

split_reasoning: Usability and functionality are subjects of the same feedback and recommendation activity.

parts.text: Provide developers with feedback and recommendations on software usability and functionality.
parts.type_reasoning: Actionable feedback is conveyed to developers as a distinct set of findings or recommendations.
parts.unit_reasoning: Feedback on a feature or review is commonly shared as a coherent set.
parts.work_item: one set of usability or functionality feedback
parts.start: software behavior or a feature is evaluated
parts.end: findings and recommendations are communicated to developers

notes: Feedback may also be given verbally during a design review.

split_reasoning: Performance monitoring is continuous, but its actionable outputs are individual performance issues investigated.

parts.text: Investigate a performance issue identified through program monitoring.
parts.type_reasoning: Each identified issue produces findings or an escalation that others can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: An observed performance issue is investigated and communicated as a unit.
parts.start: monitoring reveals a performance anomaly or threshold breach
parts.end: findings are recorded and the issue is closed or escalated
parts.checked_by: developers and operations or test lead

notes: Some workplaces also produce periodic performance summaries; the target does not specify a reporting cadence.

split_reasoning: Programs, hardware, operating systems, and networks are alternative compatibility environments for the same testing activity.

parts.text: Conduct software compatibility tests in a specified environment.
parts.type_reasoning: A compatibility test produces results for the tested configuration.
parts.unit_reasoning: Results for a defined environment or configuration are reviewed together.
parts.work_item: one compatibility test run for a configuration
parts.start: software build, configuration, and compatibility tests are ready
parts.end: tests are completed and configuration-specific results recorded

split_reasoning: Installing and configuring a recreation are connected steps in producing one testing environment.

parts.text: Set up a recreation of a software production environment for performance testing.
parts.type_reasoning: The configured environment is a distinct resource used by testers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A recreated environment is handed over for a defined testing effort.
parts.start: production configuration and test environment requirements are available
parts.end: environment is installed, configured, and checked for testing
parts.checked_by: performance testers and environment or operations team

notes: This covers software environment setup, not physical hardware installation.

split_reasoning: Collaborating with field staff on a case and assisting a customer who is present are different working contexts.

parts.text: Collaborate with field staff to diagnose a software problem and recommend solutions.
parts.type_reasoning: The joint investigation produces findings and recommendations that field staff can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: A referred problem is worked through and its findings returned as a case.
parts.work_item: one field problem evaluated with staff
parts.start: field staff raise a problem and provide available details
parts.end: diagnostic findings and possible solutions are shared with field staff

parts.text: Work with a customer during a live contact to evaluate a software problem and suggest solutions.
parts.type_reasoning: The customer participates and waits while the problem is evaluated and guidance is given.
parts.unit_reasoning: The live diagnostic contact is a bounded interaction with an outcome communicated to the customer.
parts.start: customer describes the problem during the contact
parts.end: findings or possible next steps are explained before the contact ends

notes: Customer collaboration may instead involve longer offline investigation; shares depend on the role and support model.

split_reasoning: Identifying a standards deviation and suggesting a correction are connected parts of one compliance finding.

parts.text: Identify a program's deviation from standards and suggest a modification.
parts.type_reasoning: Each finding and recommendation is an output developers or compliance reviewers can act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: A particular deviation and its suggested correction are reviewed together.
parts.start: program behavior or implementation is checked against an applicable standard
parts.end: deviation and suggested modification are documented or communicated
parts.checked_by: developers and compliance or quality lead

split_reasoning: Designing and developing an automated testing tool are connected stages of producing the tool.

parts.text: Design or develop an automated testing tool.
parts.type_reasoning: A tool or defined tool enhancement is a software deliverable used by testers.
parts.unit_reasoning: A bounded tool component or enhancement can be reviewed and handed over without treating the whole automation project as one item.
parts.work_item: one automated testing tool component or enhancement
parts.start: an automation need and requirements are identified
parts.end: component or enhancement is implemented, checked, and submitted for use

notes: A design-only assignment may hand over a specification rather than implemented code.

split_reasoning: User and third-party testing are alternative participants in the same coordination activity.

parts.text: Coordinate a round of user or third-party testing.
parts.type_reasoning: Coordination produces an organized testing round with participants, materials, and arrangements in place.
parts.unit_reasoning: A defined testing round is the unit scheduled and handed over to participating testers.
parts.work_item: one user or third-party testing round coordinated
parts.start: need, scope, and timing for external testing are identified
parts.end: participants and arrangements are confirmed and testing information is distributed

notes: Coordination includes communication with participants; executing their tests is not part of this item.

split_reasoning: Configuration files, logs, and code are alternative inputs to the same initial debugging activity.

parts.text: Perform initial debugging to identify the source of a software breakdown.
parts.type_reasoning: The investigation produces an initial diagnosis or evidence for further debugging.
parts.unit_reasoning: One breakdown is investigated and its findings handed to the responsible team.
parts.start: a software breakdown and relevant evidence are available
parts.end: likely source or remaining unknowns are recorded and communicated

split_reasoning: Visiting a beta site and evaluating performance there are connected parts of one on-site evaluation.

parts.text: Evaluate software performance at a beta testing site.
parts.type_reasoning: The site evaluation produces findings that the product team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: Findings from one site visit are normally communicated together.
parts.start: a beta site and evaluation objectives are identified
parts.end: site observations and performance findings are documented or shared

notes: Travel to a site does not by itself make the evaluation hands-on physical work.

split_reasoning: Evaluation and recommendation are connected steps in selecting testing or bug-tracking software.

parts.text: Evaluate testing or bug-tracking software and recommend an option.
parts.type_reasoning: The assessment produces a recommendation or comparison for a decision maker.
parts.unit_reasoning: A comparison for a defined tool-selection need is reviewed as a whole.
parts.work_item: one testing or bug-tracking software evaluation
parts.start: tool-selection need and evaluation criteria are identified
parts.end: evaluation findings and recommendation are submitted
parts.checked_by: test lead and software purchasing or IT decision makers

notes: An evaluation may conclude without recommending a particular product.

split_reasoning: Historical analysis is one activity applied to a selected body of test results.

parts.text: Analyze historical test results for patterns and trends.
parts.type_reasoning: The analysis produces findings that the test or project team can use.
parts.unit_reasoning: An analysis of results for a defined period, release, or question is reviewed as a whole.
parts.start: analysis question and relevant historical results are identified
parts.end: patterns and findings are summarized and shared
